chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn 'Amira, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Ibrahim ibn Shu'ayb, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'My father has aged significantly and weakened, so we carry him when he has the need.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'If you have the capacity to attend to that from him, then do so, and feed him morsels with your hand, for it will be a shield for you tomorrow.'

key_terms.تَلِيَ: To attend to, manage, or take charge of a matter
key_terms.جُنَّةٌ: Shield or protection from divine punishment or trials
key_terms.غَداً: Tomorrow (referring to the Day of Judgment or the intermediate realm)
key_terms.لَقِّمْهُ: Feed him morsels (specifically with the hand)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for caring for an elderly parent according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) specifically recommends the intimate act of feeding the father by hand, elevating physical care to a spiritual shield (junnah) against Hereafter trials. This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on active, personal service (khidmah) to parents as a means of expiating sins and securing divine protection.
